title: _photo_meta.json
description: Provenance for real photographs. One file per asset folder, keyed by filename, sitting beside the images it describes. Validated by scripts/check_assets.py.

source.description: organisation or repository the file came from

url_or_origin.description: page URL, or the project path for a PROJECT_OWNED asset

licence.description: e.g. CC BY-SA 4.0, CC0, public domain, written permission

description.description: what the photograph LITERALLY shows - not what it is used to teach. Trainees read it: it is the text of the photo's panel on every slide (L52, gb_photo.js), so write it for them - what is in the picture and where to look, in plain words, never more than the picture evidences

shows.description: L53: the plain names of the on-board things the photograph really shows, as slides and drawings name them, lower case, no abbreviations - e.g. ["fuel tank", "type C tank"], ["bunkering station"]. The compiler puts the photo beside every drawing that names one of them. Only what the picture evidences: a cargo tank of an LNG carrier is a "membrane tank", never a "fuel tank"

copied_from.description: set by the compiler when it copied the photo in from another module of the course (L53)

visually_verified.description: 'yes - <what was seen> <date>', or a plain statement that it was not verified. Never 'yes' for a file nobody opened.

caption_caveat.description: an honest near-miss note, e.g. 'a product tanker, not a gas carrier'
